To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
tau induces microtubules from R tubulin under nonassembly conditions and that the binding of tau to tubulin follows a ligand-elongation process.

tau is able, in the presence of magnesium and under nonassembly conditions, to induce ring formation from tubulin dimers, which can be converted into microtubules in the presence of guanosine 5′-triphosphate.
tau is able (i) to induce microtubule assembly from R-tubulin in phosphate buffer and (ii) to form ring-shaped structures from tubulin dimers under nonassembly conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of microtubule assembly.
the elucidation of the mechanism of microtubule assembly, and the role of tau in the regulation of this process.
the elucidation of the molecular basis of the interaction between tau and R-tubulin, a key process for microtubule assembly.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the tau-tau interaction is the driving force for tubulin-tubulin interaction, which leads to the formation of the microtubule.
tau is able, under nonassembly conditions, to form microtubule-like structures from tubulin dimers.
tau is able, under specific conditions, to induce tubulin polymerization in a nonassembly system, without the presence of magnesium and GTP.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
tau induces ring and microtubule assembly from R tubulin under nonassembly conditions and this process is mediated by a ligand-mediated mechanism.

tau induces ring and microtubule assembly from R tubulin in nonassembly conditions, and this process requires both the C-terminal regions of R- and a tubulin, and is not accompanied by a global folding of the protein.
tau induces ring and microtubule assembly from tubulin dimers under nonassembly conditions by means of a ligand-mediated mechanism, with a binding site on the C-terminal region of tubulin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
tau can bind and stabilize R tubulin under nonassembly conditions and that this binding can lead to the formation of rings and microtubules.
tau is able not only to bind to R tubulin in the absence of magnesium but also to induce microtubule assembly from R tubulin.
tau is able, under nonassembly conditions, to induce both micro-tubule and ring formations from tubulin dimers.
